name: Central Polydactyly

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Central Polydactyly

criteria.description: Presence of one or more duplicated central digits (index, middle, or ring finger/toe)
Radiographic evidence of duplicated phalanges or metacarpals/metatarsals in central rays
No clinical or genetic evidence of syndromic polydactyly or other limb malformations

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of duplicated central digits confirmed clinically and radiographically
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may be used to exclude syndromic causes; diagnosis primarily clinical and radiological

pathognomonic.symptomName: Duplicated central digits of the hand or foot
searchTerms: extra middle fingers or toes
central finger or toe duplication

pathognomonic.symptomName: Central ray duplication involving metacarpal or metatarsal bones
searchTerms: extra central hand or foot bones
duplicated middle metacarpal or metatarsal
webbing between duplicated fingers or toes
fused skin between extra digits

common.symptomName: Mild functional impairment of affected hand or foot
searchTerms: slight difficulty using affected hand or foot
mild movement problems in duplicated digits

common.symptomName: Soft tissue mass or prominence at duplication site
searchTerms: soft lump where extra digit is
mass at duplication site

common.symptomName: Nail duplication or malformation on duplicated digits
searchTerms: extra or misshapen nails on duplicated digits
nail abnormalities on extra fingers or toes
stiff joints in affected fingers or toes
limited joint flexibility in duplicated digits

occasional.symptomName: Mild pain or discomfort during digit movement
searchTerms: mild pain when moving extra digits
discomfort during finger or toe movement

occasional.symptomName: Cosmetic concerns related to digit duplication
searchTerms: concerns about appearance of extra digits
cosmetic issues from digit duplication

occasional.symptomName: Limited range of motion in duplicated digits
searchTerms: reduced movement range in duplicated fingers or toes
limited digit flexibility
unequal limb lengths
one limb longer than the other
blood flow or nerve problems in extra digits
circulation or nerve issues in duplicated fingers or toes

rare.symptomName: Infection or ulceration at duplication site
searchTerms: infection or sores at extra digit site
ulcers on duplicated digits

imaging: X-ray showing duplicated phalanges and metacarpals/metatarsals in central rays
MRI may be used to assess soft tissue involvement
genetic: Genetic testing to exclude syndromic polydactyly (e.g., GLI3 mutations)
other: Physical examination revealing duplicated central digits with or without syndactyly

distinguishingFeatures: Duplication of thumb or great toe rather than central digits
Different genetic mutations and clinical presentation
Duplication of fifth digit (ulnar or fibular side)
Usually involves different anatomical and radiological features
Presence of additional systemic features (e.g., craniofacial anomalies, cardiac defects)
Genetic mutations associated with syndromes such as Greig cephalopolysyndactyly

redFlags: Presence of systemic anomalies suggesting syndromic polydactyly
Neurovascular compromise or ischemia of duplicated digits
Rapidly progressive swelling or signs of infection at duplication site
references: Temtamy SA, McKusick VA. The Genetics of Hand Malformations. 1978.
Goldfarb CA, Manske PR. Polydactyly: Classification and Treatment. J Am Acad Orthop Surg. 2006.
